frontmatter.title: Getting Started

blocks.content: Aspose.3D for TypeScript enables developers to load, process, and convert 3D models directly in Node.js or browser-based applications. By the end of this guide, you will be able to import 3D assets such as OBJ and FBX files into a scene, inspect their geometry, and prepare them for rendering or further manipulation in a typescript 3d library workflow.

The library supports rich 3d formats including OBJ with full material and coordinate data, and FBX with scene hierarchy, animation, and textures. Using the `Scene` class and format-specific importers like `ObjImporter`, you can programmatically access mesh vertices, polygons, and materials—ideal for 3d typescript game engine integration or visualization pipelines.
To use Aspose.3D with TypeScript, ensure you have Node.js 16 or later installed. Install the package via npm using the command `npm install Aspose.3D`. No additional system dependencies are required.

items: Basic familiarity with TypeScript and 3D concepts (e.g., scenes, nodes, meshes)

blocks.content: This guide walks you through loading a 3D model in TypeScript using Aspose.3D. You’ll import a GLTF 2.0 file with PBR materials, inspect its structure, and verify successful loading by outputting mesh data. This workflow demonstrates core capabilities of the typescript 3d library, including support for node hierarchies, mesh primitives, and texture references as defined in the GLTF 2.0 specification.
Begin by installing the package via npm. Aspose.3D requires TypeScript 5.0 or later, ensuring compatibility with modern tooling and type safety.
Create a new `Scene` instance and open a GLTF file. The library supports full GLTF 2.0 with PBR materials, node transforms, and mesh primitives.
Traverse the scene’s node hierarchy to access mesh entities. For each node with an attached mesh, log its name and geometry statistics.

This example demonstrates how to create a simple 3D scene and export it to GLTF 2.0 format using Aspose.3D in a TypeScript environment. It assumes Node.js 16+, 18+, 20+, or 22+ is installed, as required by the library. The code constructs a basic scene with a cube, then saves it as a .gltf file—showcasing the library’s GLTF export capability.
After installing Aspose.3D for TypeScript, explore these resources to deepen your understanding and accelerate development with 3D models in modern browsers.
